clue.text: Has its point in figured work

definitions.text: Has its point in figured work

parts.words: Has its point in figured work
parts.note: a kind of number written with a dot separating whole units from tenths and hundredths, used in arithmetic or 'figure work'

explanation.surface: Something whose purpose lies in a piece of ornamental, patterned work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' reads as purpose and 'figured' as decorated, but the point is the dot in a number and figured work is sums.
explanation.definitionFit: Base-ten fractions are written with a dot, the point, separating the whole part, as in arithmetic sums.

clue.text: Throw her a towel by the pool

indicators.note: to throw something is to toss it about, so the letters of the following words are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to toss a towel to a woman lounging beside the swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw' rearranges HER A TOWEL; 'by the' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pond or small natural pool where animals come to drink is the sense meant.

clue.text: Got fire going again around the reactor core — thus, an old widow!

indicators.note: around means the rekindling word goes round the outside of the core letter

parts.note: to get a fire going again is to light it again, past tense relit

indicators.note: the core of a word is its central letter, here the middle of reactor

explanation.surface: A nuclear-flavoured scene of rekindled fire, ending in an exclamation about an aged widow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts C, the middle letter of 'reactor', inside RELIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A relict is an old-fashioned legal or literary term for a surviving spouse, especially a widow.

clue.text: Caption is ingenious, including it

indicators.note: including means the word for clever holds the next word within it

parts.note: subtle can mean clever or ingenious, as in a subtle plan

explanation.surface: A remark that some caption is clever, and contains a certain word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' is the container signal; 'is' links. 'ingenious' gives the adjective, which wraps the pronoun in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Film and television text lines at the bottom of the screen are captions translating dialogue.

clue.text: To become taller, take exercise

definitions.meaning: read literally, lengthening your lower limbs would make you taller
the idiom means to go for a walk after sitting still

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means going for a stroll after sitting a long time; taken literally, lengthening limbs adds height.

clue.text: Always turning up?

parts.note: describes an unwanted person or thing that keeps reappearing, from the saying about a worthless coin that always comes back

explanation.walkthrough: The British saying 'turns up like a ...' describes someone unwelcome who keeps coming back; 'turning up' also suggests a coin face up.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says an unwelcome person reappears like a worthless coin you can never get rid of.

clue.text: Just ticked aver, though had been in front

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Just ticked aver, though had been in front': 'aver' is likely 'over' (IDLED = ticked over), but the remaining wordplay needs I'D LED and no clue word supplies the I
annotationWithheld.clue: Just ticked aver, though had been in front

clue.text: Badly leaking connection

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of the next word are put together wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint about a joint or pipe connection that leaks badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' rearranges LEAKING.
explanation.definitionFit: A system of links joining parts together is a connection, as in a mechanical coupling.

clue.text: Deteriorated, it's said, over a long period.

indicators.note: it's said means the word for deteriorated is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to deteriorate is to rot or decay, past tense decayed

explanation.surface: Something that slowly fell apart over many years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's said' signals a homophone of DECAYED; 'over a' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten years is a lengthy stretch of time.

clue.text: Smelling a rat, the Spaniard snarled

indicators.note: snarled means tangled up, so the letters are knotted into a new order

parts.note: a rat is an example of a rodent
el is Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: A suspicious Spaniard senses a rat and snarls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snarled' rearranges RODENT + EL. Spanish words in clues are a convention: 'the Spaniard' means 'the' in Spanish.
explanation.definitionFit: Redolent of something means smelling strongly of it, as in a room redolent of garlic.

clue.text: Not the main track for the team

parts.note: a side is a sports team
a line is a railway track

explanation.surface: A remark about a branch railway track used by a sports team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not the main' is the definition; 'for' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A secondary activity or occupation, as opposed to one's primary job.

clue.text: Being close to the listener, win favour

parts.note: close as a noun is the end, as in the close of day
the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: Getting near someone to whisper and win their approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' looks like an adjective meaning near, but it is the noun meaning end.
explanation.definitionFit: To make oneself liked or win affection is the sense, as in endearing oneself to a person.

clue.text: Feeble member of the family with the nervous twitch

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father
taken as written
a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: A weak relative afflicted with a nervous twitch.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'with' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathetic is used for something weak or inadequate, as in a pathetic excuse.

clue.text: Partly prevented deer fouling reed

parts.note: a hind is a female deer

indicators.note: fouling means messing up, so the letters of the plant word are jumbled

explanation.surface: Deer messing up reed beds, partly preventing something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fouling' makes ERED from the plant word; 'Partly prevented' is the definition, partly hindering being a fair sense of obstruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindered means obstructed or held back, stopping something from going freely.

clue.text: Duck and swallow under cover

parts.note: the eider is a sea duck
to down a drink is to swallow it

explanation.surface: A duck and a swallow sheltering under cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallow' looks like a bird beside the duck, but is the verb; 'under' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A quilt stuffed with soft feathers, originally from a sea duck, is a bed covering.

clue.text: Celebrates vehicles crossing the river

indicators.note: crossing means the vehicles span the river, sitting either side of it

parts.note: cars are vehicles
the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: Vehicles driving over a river bridge in celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' is the container signal: the vehicles straddle the Yorkshire river, as cars on a bridge would.
explanation.definitionFit: To carouse is to drink and make merry, a noisy celebration.

clue.text: Cry of course will make us aware of imminent shot

definitions.text: Cry of course will make us aware of imminent shot

parts.words: Cry of course will make us aware of imminent shot
parts.note: the golfer's shout on a golf course, warning of a ball on its way, gives advance notice of the shot

explanation.surface: A shout on the golf course warning of a ball heading our way.
explanation.walkthrough: The golf warning shout 'fore' plus 'warn' gives the word; 'course' means a golf course, not 'naturally'.
explanation.definitionFit: To alert someone in advance of danger, as the golfing shout does.

clue.text: Former pupils smoke — why, it isn't clear

definitions.note: a clause where the answer is an adjective; obscure describes something that isn't clear

parts.note: OBs are old boys, former pupils of a school
to cure fish or meat is to preserve it, often by smoking

explanation.surface: Old school pupils smoking, and nobody knows why.
explanation.walkthrough: OB, old boy, is British for a former pupil of a school. 'why' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscure means hard to make out or understand, not plain.

clue.text: Ducks taxes without hesitation

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the tax word goes round the hesitation

parts.note: scot is an old word for a tax, as in scot-free
er is a hesitation sound

explanation.surface: Someone dodging taxes without a moment's hesitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' in its old sense of outside is the container signal. 'Ducks' looks like a verb (dodges) but names the birds; scot survives in scot-free.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoters are dark sea ducks of northern waters.

clue.text: Cardinal point

definitions.meaning: a cardinal of the Catholic Church is addressed as His ...
a high point of land, a rise or summit

explanation.definitionFit: The title for a senior Catholic churchman, and a piece of rising ground.

clue.text: Makes slow progress of some feet

definitions.meaning: to edge forward bit by bit
units of length, twelve to a foot, so parts of some feet

explanation.definitionFit: To edge along gradually; also small units of length, twelve to a foot.

clue.text: Does change include copper coin?

indicators.note: include means the rearranged letters hold the chemical symbol within them
change signals that the letters of the word before it are altered into another order

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A question about whether loose change contains a copper coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' makes ESDO from 'Does' and 'include' is the container signal. 'change' and 'coin' suggest money, which disguises the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The escudo was the currency unit of Portugal before the euro.

clue.text: Someone to bring the lady to us

definitions.text: Someone to bring the lady to us

parts.note: taken as written
her is the pronoun for a lady

explanation.surface: Asking for someone to show a woman over to where we sit.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the job and also builds it: 'the lady' is HER, joined to US.
explanation.definitionFit: An attendant who shows guests to their seats brings people to where others are.

clue.text: Sanity exemplified by girl embracing idiot, but without love

indicators.note: embracing means the girl's name holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: Lucy is a girl's name

indicators.note: without means a letter is dropped from idiot

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A girl hugging a fool, but not loving him, shows good sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' makes IDIT by dropping love's letter, and 'embracing' is the container signal; 'exemplified by' and 'but' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucidity means clear-headedness, a sound and rational mind.

clue.text: High-ranking lady starting to eat centre-piece at table

parts.note: a duchess is a noblewoman of high rank

indicators.note: starting to means only the first letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A noblewoman about to eat sits at the centre of the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starting to' takes E from 'eat'. The definition names a table cover or set of mats laid in the middle of a table.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative cloth or set of mats laid on a dressing or dining table takes this French name.

clue.text: Performed war dance — and he took part

indicators.note: took part means a part of the words is taken, the name lying inside them

explanation.surface: Someone performed a war dance and a man joined in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took part' pulls the name out of performED WARDance; 'he' is the definition, a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A male first name stands for a man, which the pronoun refers to.

clue.text: Dresser ought to be set off, with them

definitions.text: Dresser ought to be set off, with them

indicators.note: set off means started up or shaken loose, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: ought, as a form of nought, is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A dressing table should be decorated with flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be set off' rearranges DRESSER + O; read whole, the clue says a dresser is shown off with flowers on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimson blooms set on a dressing table show it off.
